DANIEL'S OBJECTIVE: to be forgiven — and he knows he has no right to
ask, so he asks with the smallest thing he has. STATUS: low, and it is
in the body — the head slightly down, the shoulders in, the hand going
to his own face (wiping the rain is really self-touching), the eyes
coming up to hers and dropping again. He says the line QUIETLY, almost
swallowing it: the quietest thing in the scene, because he does not
believe it will work. And it is on that line that he dares to move: the
walk toward her is slow, careful, a man approaching something that
might bolt — never a stride, never a lunge, each step placed. When
nothing comes back from her he stops apologising and just walks —
the chin dropping, the eyes going to the ground for a step. That small
collapse, walked, is the beat. He stops an arm's length from her and
waits.
REBECCA'S OBJECTIVE: to hold on to herself — and she loses. She has
been upright and defended all night; here the defence fails. It shows
first in the body, before the words: the shoulders coming down, the
hand going to her wet hair and pushing it back twice for nothing. Her
line comes out BROKEN — a false start, a hesitation, an unfinished edge
— the way a real person says something they have not said before. She
is not telling him off and she is not asking for anything: she is
admitting she has lost her bearings, and admitting it out loud makes it
true, which is why her mouth stays open after it. STATUS BREAK: the
woman who refused him all night has just given him something, and she
knows it. She does not go to him and does not back away: she stays at
the edge, her hand on the brick, and lets him come.
THE TWO SILENCES ARE EVENTS, NOT HOLES: in his, he waits for a reaction
and receives none, and folds a little while still walking. In hers, she
registers what she has just admitted and does not withdraw it.

apart, nobody steps, nobody turns, nobody reaches, nobody touches; two
soaked people looking at each other with nothing decided.

on each other, and neither ever looks up, at the sky, at the fallen

and neither of them can speak on a steady voice. Living eyes for both —
natural blinks, gaze shifting with intent, real catch-lights. No
